key_claim: Farming let humans build cities, states and writing, but early farmers often lived harder, less healthy lives than foragers.

slides.headline: Farming built civilisation. It also made life harder.
It started in many places
slides.body: About 12,000 years ago, people in several parts of the world began farming on their own. It was not one idea that spread.

slides.headline: More food, harder lives
slides.body: Farming fed far more people. But early farmers were often shorter, had worse teeth and caught more diseases than foragers.

slides.headline: Writing began as bookkeeping
slides.body: Around 3200 BCE, the Sumerians began writing to track grain and taxes. Many early tablets just count barley and beer.

caption:
Farming built civilisation. It also made life harder.

1. Farming began on its own in several places, about 12,000 years ago.
2. It fed far more people, but early farmers were often less healthy than foragers.
3. Writing began around 3200 BCE as a way to track grain and taxes.

Source: Waypoint — The Agricultural Revolution
